files.why: Add a runtime read model (e.g. fetchRescheduleEnabled(customerId)) hitting a settings/entitlements endpoint so the flag is fetched at request time, never baked in at build/deploy.
Add the server-shape (snake_case) DTO schema for the entitlement/settings response; DTOs must stay in data/.
Map the entitlement DTO to a core-friendly value so the raw DTO never leaks upward into ui/core.
Add an MSW handler returning the flag keyed per customer, so it can actually be flipped on/off in the mock backend without a redeploy.
Thread the entitlement into canReschedule/validateReschedule so the pure domain is the single source of truth for whether the flow is permitted and owns the user-facing message.
New composable that loads the entitlement for the current customer and exposes it reactively to the view (the ui-boundary that reads runtime state).
Accept the entitlement and pass it into validateReschedule so submit() also refuses when the flow is off, not just the button being hidden.
Consume the flag to show/hide the Reschedule button and RescheduleForm — the only UI surface that renders the reschedule flow.

uncertain: Whether the fetch belongs in the existing data/queries.ts or a new data/entitlements.ts file — both are architecturally legal; queries.ts matches convention but this is arguably a distinct concern.

Whether a single boolean warrants the full DTO+mapper(+core type) ceremony, or whether it should also gain a core/types.ts entry to name the read model; the repo maps even trivial fields, so I leaned faithful over minimal.

Whether to add a dedicated useRescheduleEnabled composable or fold the flag load into the existing useDaySchedule — a separate composable keeps day-loading and entitlement concerns apart, but is one more file.
Whether RescheduleForm.vue also needs its own guard (belt-and-suspenders); I left it out because the button is hidden and core/policy refuses, but a reviewer may want it explicit.
Whether this should stay in-slice (rule 7: one feature, keep it in scheduling) or is the first of many per-customer entitlements that would justify a shared/app-level entitlements layer later.
questions: What does 'per customer' mean here — the tenant/business using Vise, or the end-client (clientId like c-ana)? The app currently has no tenant/auth/session identity at all, and DayView isn't even client-scoped, so there is no customer id to key the flag on today.

Where does the on/off switch actually live server-side (feature-flag service, settings endpoint, entitlements API) and what is the endpoint path + response shape? The frontend can only read it; the real toggle must exist server-side for 'without deploying' to hold.
When the flag is off, should the reschedule UI be hidden entirely, or shown disabled with an explanatory message?
Refresh/caching expectations: is a normal fetch on view load enough, or must a flip take effect live (polling / cache invalidation) without a page reload?
Is this genuinely scheduling-only, or the first of several per-customer entitlements — which would change whether we build it in-slice now or invest in a reusable entitlements mechanism?
